1  THIS WP IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 & 227 OF THE  CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO QUASH THE GENERAL  AWARD DATED 23.03.2013 BEARING NO.BENGALURU/VIBHUSWAAA-  2//2012-13 PASSED BY THE R3 VIDE ANNEXURE-A, DIRECT THE  RESPONDENTS TO CONSIDER THE CASE OF THE PETITIONER AS PER  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:40188  WP No. 24733 of 2023 SECTION 29(2) OF THE KIAD ACT FOR PASSING THE CONSENT AWARD IN RESPECT OF PETITIONERS LAND MEASURING 10 GUNTAS IN SY.NO.107 SITUATED AT AREHALLI GUDDADAHALLI VILLAGE,
KASABA HOBLI, DODDABALLAPURA TALUK, BENGALURU RURAL DISTRICT.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(i) Issue a writ in the nature of certiorari quashing the General Award dated 23.03.2013 bearing No.Bengaluru / ViBhuSwaAa-2 / 2012-13 passed by the 3rd respondent vide Annexure-A;
(ii) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act for petitioner's land measuring 10 guntas in Sy.no.107 situated at Arehalli Guddadahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District and etc.
2.

Sri Shrihari A.V., learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner was absolute owner of land bearing Sy.no.107, measuring 10 guntas situated at Arehalli Guddadahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, which was sought to be acquired by respondent - authorities for III Stage of Apparel Park Project.
3. It was submitted that petitioner had no objection for acquisition of land by respondents - KIADB,
but without issuing notice and granting opportunity to petitioner to avail NC: 2023:KHC:40188 compensation under consent award, General Award was passed.
Since compensation under consent award was higher than under General Award, denial was contrary to law.

4. It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court in W.P.no.22547/2023 disposed of on 27.10.2023 and several other cases, had held such denial as unsustainable, quashed General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's representation for passing consent award.
Hence sought for passing similar order.

Smt. Gowramma vs The State Of Karanataka on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56185504/
2 5.

sentences.text: Sri Yogesh D. Naik, learned AGA for respondent no.1 and Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that in view of earlier decisions, respondent no.3 would consider petitioner's representation, if petitioner furnished relevant documents in support of his claim over property acquired and sought for disposal of writ petition.
6. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
7. From above, it is seen that only reason for not availing compensation under consent award is due to failure in NC: 2023:KHC:40188 producing records to substantiate title.
Therefore, if petitioner produced same, there would be no impediment for respondents to consider petitioner's claim for passing consent award.

On perusal of order passed in W.P.no.22547/2023 disposed of on 27.10.2023, it is seen that under similar circumstances, this Court had set aside General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's representation for passing consent award.
Said decision would also squarely apply in this case.

Consequently, writ petition is disposed of by setting aside General Award bearing no.Bengaluru/ViBhuSwaAa-2/2012-13 dated 23.03.2013 vide Annexure-A passed by respondent no.3, insofar as it relates to of petitioner's land measuring 10 guntas in Sy.no.107, situated at Arehalli Guddadahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.

Petitioner is permitted to submit documents to establish title insofar as his property under acquisition and thereafter respondent no.3 - SLAO shall consider same for passing consent award,
within a period of eight weeks from date of receipt certified copy of this order.

NC: 2023:KHC:40188 It is clarified that in case of dispute regarding title over acquired property,
General Award passed, though quashed herein, would revive.
Liberty is reserved to respondent no.3 to withdraw proportionate compensation deposited before Reference Court for said purpose.

Sd/-
